newsitem.title: USA: Land O'Lakes, Atlantic Dairy Co-op set merger.
newsitem.headline: Land O'Lakes, Atlantic Dairy Co-op set merger.

text.p: Food and agricultural cooperative Land O'Lakes said it would merge with Atlantic Dairy Cooperative, a Pennsylvania-based milk marketer.
The agreement, announced Thursday at the Land O'Lakes annual meeting here, will be effective April 1, 1997. The organizations will be continue under the Land O'Lakes name.
The pact is subject to approval by Atlantic Dairy members at a vote scheduled for March 13.
The two cooperatives have been business partners since 1980 when Atlantic began producing butter for Land O'Lakes at its Holly Milk facility near Carlisle, Pa.
Atlantic Dairy, with 3,600 producer-members in seven mid-Atlantic states, is one of Land O'Lakes' largest members.

"We are excited about this opportunity to maximize our butter supply close to our strongest markets while establishing a true national organization with membership on the East Coast, across the Midwest and reaching to the West Coast," said John Gherty, president and chief executive officer of Land O'Lakes.
Terms of the merger were not announced.

Land O'Lakes is a Minnesota-based cooperative owned by farmers, ranchers and member cooperatives in 20 states. It provides agricultural inputs to nearly 1,000 member cooperatives supplying 300,000 farmers and manufactures and markets a wide variety of food products.
